# See your service in the graph and in wallets

Once trusted, your service is discoverable. This is how to look at yourself the way others do.

## In the graph

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://graph.testnet.verana.network/v4/graph/search -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"surface":"Did","q":"Example Company","limit":5}' | jq '.items[] | {did, snippet}'
curl -s -X POST https://graph.testnet.verana.network/v4/graph/traverse -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"A1","input":{"did":"did:webvh:…"}}' | jq
```

Search returns a snippet card: your service and operator claims, your accreditations, your endpoints. The trust summary traversal (`A1`) shows the chain behind each credential. The [search UI](https://search.testnet.verana.network) renders the same.

## In wallets

Every integrated wallet renders the same five blocks: the verdict, your service (name, type, logo, description), who operates it (name, country, registry id), your other credentials, and the chain behind each. What people see is your claims; give them a square logo that reads at 40 pixels, a description that says what the service does, real terms and privacy pages.

## Improving

A claim change means a new credential: update the configuration and obtain a new Organization credential or re-issue the Service credential. The agent handles the republication; the indexer re-evaluates on your next trigger.
